behavioral_notes.observation: The universal RPC dispatch of the whole client. Every model method the browser invokes goes through this single jsonrpc route: it resolves request.registry[model], then delegates to odoo.service.model.call_kw(env[model], method, args, kwargs). readonly is computed dynamically by walking the model MRO for a method-level _readonly flag, which routes the request to a read-replica cursor when possible. This is the metadata-invisible heart of Odoo's frontend-to-ORM bridge.

The web client bootstrap. ensure_db() + session.uid checks gate access, security.check_session validates the session (raising SessionExpiredException), user._on_webclient_bootstrap() runs, then ir.http.webclient_rendering_context() builds session_info and the page renders the 'web.webclient_bootstrap' QWeb template with Cache-Control: no-store and X-Frame-Options: DENY. This template is what loads the entire OWL asset bundle that becomes the SPA.

Session handling: authenticate() opens a fresh Registry cursor/Environment, calls request.session.authenticate(env, credential), persists session.db and saves the session, then returns ir.http.session_info(). get_session_info() touches the session (refreshing lifetime) and re-returns session_info. /web/session/account builds an Odoo OAuth2 URL (accounts.odoo.com) from database.uuid. These wire browser session state to server-side auth, invisible to ORM metadata.

web is the prime example of metadata gap #3: it ships the ENTIRE client framework as static assets, not Python models. extract_frontend.py finds ~526 JS files and ~257 XML/QWeb templates, 40+ catalogued OWL components, dozens of registry categories (actions, fields, services, dialogs, error_handlers, color_picker_tabs), core services (orm_service, name_service, field_service, rpc, registry) and ~30 asset bundles (web.assets_backend=66, web.assets_frontend=67, web.report_assets_common=52). static/src/start.js mounts the WebClient OWL root onto document.body. None of this is reverse-engineerable from Python metadata.

it_architecture.application: web (Web Client framework / WSGI app, asset bundler, OWL SPA host)
information_flows: bridge: browser OWL client -> /web/dataset/call_kw -> odoo.service.model.call_kw -> ORM (any model/method)
bootstrap: /web|/odoo -> ir.http.webclient_rendering_context -> render web.webclient_bootstrap -> load asset bundles -> mount WebClient (start.js)
extends: ir.http, ir.ui.view, ir.ui.menu, ir.model, ir.qweb.field.* (routing, views, menus, qweb rendering)

capabilities: Render the Application UI (OWL Single-Page Web Client)
Provide the Field/View/Service/Registry Framework all modules extend
value_streams: Request-to-Render: browser request -> bootstrap -> asset bundle -> mounted OWL client
Action-to-View: load_menus/action.load -> view rendering -> call_kw data fetch -> rendered records
policies: 2 record rules (minimal); web client bootstrap enforces session/security.check_session and is_user_internal gating; Cache-Control: no-store + X-Frame-Options: DENY on the client page
stakeholders: End user (every authenticated user renders through this layer)
metrics: Profiling / speedscope endpoints (/web/set_profiling, /web/speedscope) for client/server performance traces

classification.rationale: web is technical/firm infrastructure (Porter support activity; Stabell & Fjeldstad 'support'). It is not a value-creating primary activity of any single value chain/shop/network — it is the UI framework and HTTP/RPC plumbing that EVERY other module renders and dispatches through. auto_install=true makes it ubiquitous infrastructure. Its substance is the FRONTEND (~526 JS / ~257 XML, the OWL framework, registries and services) plus 68 routes, with only ~2 real Python models — the exact inverse of a data-bearing business module. APQC 8.0 'Manage Information Technology' fits because web is the IT-delivery/application-platform capability (develop & manage application software, deliver the UI runtime); 13.0 'Develop and Manage Business Capabilities' was considered (web is the platform other capabilities build on) but rejected because web is a concrete running runtime/application platform, not a governance/portfolio-management capability — its work is IT delivery, which is squarely 8.0.

standard_capabilities: OWL-based single-page web client (backend & frontend asset bundles)
Universal RPC bridge (/web/dataset/call_kw) to any ORM method
Field/view/widget registry framework reused by all modules
Session & authentication bootstrap, including Odoo OAuth account link
typical_fits: Standard backend client for all apps with zero per-module UI plumbing
Adding a new field widget / view type via registry registration
Patching existing OWL components via web's patch mechanism
common_gaps: Custom OWL components / services beyond the registry (requires JS dev, gap #3)
Branding / white-label theming of the client
Bespoke client-side caching or offline behavior beyond the PWA service worker
External integrations are not in web itself (gap #7) — only Odoo OAuth + CDN libs
drive_hints: curl -X POST /web/dataset/call_kw with {model:'res.partner',method:'search_read'} (auth=user) to exercise the universal RPC dispatch
odoo shell: env['ir.http'].session_info() to see the session_info payload the client bootstraps from
GET /web (browser) -> view source -> confirm web.webclient_bootstrap loads web.assets_backend bundle
GET /web/manifest.webmanifest to see the PWA manifest
